title: Puffin-D predicts excess transcription initiation in native over shuffled human DNA mostly at promoters and cCREs; outside them the excess is small or absent against 4-mer-preserving nulls
abstract: The extra transcription start sites that the Puffin-D sequence model predicts in the native human genome, compared with shuffled or reversed DNA, are mostly at gene promoters and candidate regulatory elements (cCREs); outside them the excess becomes small or disappears when the null keeps the local 4-base composition. This matters because a 2026 study (Adey et al., Genome Biology and Evolution) used this native-versus-random excess as evidence that pervasive transcription exceeds noise. Of the 2.19 million start sites that the study published, 75% lie within 1 kb of an annotated gene start and 19.5% in ENCODE cCREs; 0.21% lie in background DNA (40.6% of the genome; no annotated element nearby). In 350 windows from chromosomes that the model did not train on, 98-108% of the native-minus-null excess was in promoters, cCREs, exons and conserved elements. The excess was about 400-fold against reversal, 3.6-fold against a local dinucleotide shuffle and 1.6-fold against a local 4-mer shuffle (a shuffle that keeps the count of every 4-base word). In all DNA outside promoters, exons and conserved elements, native/4-mer-shuffle ratios were 1.21 (95% CI 0.86-1.75) for start-site clusters and 1.30 (0.98-1.72) for total signal (1.53, 1.10-2.09, with lncRNA and other gene promoters included). Background DNA alone had less predicted initiation than its own shuffles (0.31, 0.21-0.45), but this is expected because background DNA is defined by the absence of biochemical marks. On training chromosomes the model over-predicts cCRE initiation relative to measured GRO-cap data (held-out chromosomes rank lowest 3 of 22; P = 1/1540), which inflates the genome-wide count by about 15%. Measured data agree on location: background DNA holds 0.5% of measured start sites with at least 6 reads. Measured start sites in background DNA are as conserved in 241 mammals as matched control DNA (mean phyloP difference +0.003, -0.007 to +0.014). Thus the native-versus-shuffled contrast mostly measures known promoter and enhancer signals and the composition the null removes; it does not show initiation above composition-level noise outside annotated elements. Limitations: apart from GRO-cap comparisons the values are model predictions; annotation-defined compartments bias tests inside background DNA; thresholds were chosen after first results. We give a laboratory test with designed DNA.

display.caption: Where transcription start sites (TSSs) fall in the hg38 autosomes. A: share of genome bases, of the 2.19 million Puffin-D TSS positions published by Adey et al. 2026 for the native genome (lifted from T2T-CHM13), and of 4.32 million measured GM12878 GRO-cap TSS positions, in six compartments. Background DNA is 40.6% of the genome but holds 0.2% of predicted and 2.9% of measured TSSs. B: TSS positions per kb by compartment for Puffin-D on held-out chromosomes 8-10, on training chromosomes, and for measured GRO-cap (log scale).

Native versus null sequences in Puffin-D held-out windows. A: share of the native-minus-null excess of predicted TSS positions (GRO-cap output, at least 1 pseudo-read) by compartment, for reversal and local dinucleotide shuffle (the nulls of Adey et al.) and a local 4-mer shuffle; 350 windows from test chromosomes 8-9. B-D: native/null ratio of predicted TSS clusters (at least 0.5 pseudo-reads) with 95% window-bootstrap intervals in protein-coding promoters (B), in all DNA outside promoters, exons and conserved elements (C), and in background DNA (D). Background-only nulls in D pool 350 main and 1,000 background-rich held-out windows; the depletion in D is expected because background DNA is defined by the absence of biochemical marks. A ratio below 1 means less predicted initiation in the native sequence than in the null.

Conservation in 241 mammals (Zoonomia phyloP, aligned bases) within 40 bp of TSS sites relative to control spans of the same compartment, G+C and repeat status within 50 kb, for Puffin-D sites published by Adey et al. 2026 (blue) and measured GM12878 GRO-cap sites with at least 2 reads (orange). Left: mean phyloP difference. Right: ratio of the fraction of bases with phyloP of at least 2.27. Bars: 95% intervals from a bootstrap over 1-Mb blocks. Measured sites in background DNA are about as conserved as matched background DNA; sites in cCREs are more conserved; measured sites in protein-coding promoters are less conserved than other promoter DNA.
